goal: Minimize first-token latency for the source's interactive workload (batch 1, prompt 256 tokens, full greedy generation of 32 new tokens), preserving the source model, inputs, completion semantics and full quality requirements.
entrypoint: adapter.py, reproducing one timed infer() invocation of the source entry qwen_inference.py (main -> infer, qwen_inference.py:14-41); the request freezes the single 'interactive' workload row from workloads.json.
completion: One invocation completes the full frozen workload exactly as source infer(): a single prefill forward over the whole prompt (use_cache=True, logits_to_keep=1), greedy first token = argmax of the last-position logits, with the source's explicit torch.cuda.synchronize() first-token-ready boundary terminating the ttft_ms objective, then the fixed loop of new_tokens-1 = 31 cached single-token decode steps producing exactly 32 new tokens in total, ended by the source's final torch.cuda.synchronize(). EOS early stopping is disabled by the explicit loop; generation never stops before 32 tokens. Model loading, tokenization, reference capture, verification, warmup, repeats and median reduction are outside the timed invocation.
state_protocol: prepare(context, request) runs outside timing: it applies common.configure()'s numerical policy (threads 4/1, torch.manual_seed(20261020), matmul/cudnn TF32 off, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', cudnn.benchmark False) with torch.cuda.set_device(context['device']), loads the tokenizer and Qwen3ForCausalLM (bfloat16, attn_implementation='sdpa', local_files_only) from request['assets'].assets onto context['device'], builds the input by applying the chat template to the workloads.json qwen_inference.prompt (add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=False, encoded without special tokens, repeated/truncated to exactly request['workload'].prompt_tokens and tiled to batch), and keeps model/tokenizer/inputs/workload/quality in state; workload dimensions are read from request['workload'], never embedded as constants. reset(state) is effectively a no-op for this stateless greedy inference: the model is in eval/inference mode and immutable, inputs are fixed, KV caches are created per invocation inside run(), and the source clears nothing inside its timed invocation; reset only drops quality-mode capture references and synchronizes, without touching the allocator. run(state) executes the entire workload under torch.inference_mode() via the verbatim source infer() body (capture only in quality mode) and returns the generated tokens, optional per-step last-position logits, and the source's internal phase timings including the first-token boundary. observe(state, result) reruns the teacher-forced capture outside the timer, applies the source's relational checks (torch.equal greedy-token equality, logits closeness at the request tolerances, +1 corruption rejection) and returns the full tokens/logits tensors plus exact boolean/integer check results, raising on violation. metrics(state, result, elapsed_ms) exposes ttft_ms from run's internal first-token boundary plus the source's other per-sample metrics, wall-clock derived throughput and peak_allocated_bytes queried outside the timer. models(state) returns {'model': loaded Qwen3ForCausalLM}. set_mode(state, mode) toggles logits capture ('quality') versus the clean timing path ('measure'/'profile') with identical execution semantics and identical work; before_run is not needed for this single-process workload.
invariants: Greedy argmax decoding over exactly new_tokens=32 steps with EOS early stopping disabled by the explicit decode loop; the full 32-token sequence must be produced every invocation (qwen_inference.py:25-33; request.json note on input construction: 'Generation length is fixed at new_tokens=32; EOS early stopping is disabled by the explicit loop').

The workload shape is the source's infer() structure: one prefill forward over the full 256-token prompt with use_cache=True and logits_to_keep=1, first token from argmax of last-position logits, then 31 single-token decode steps reusing past_key_values with logits_to_keep=1 (qwen_inference.py:18-32).

ttft_ms is measured at the source's actual completion boundary: perf_counter_ns around prefill forward + argmax terminated by an explicit torch.cuda.synchronize() ('explicit first-token-ready boundary'); decode timing starts only after that boundary (qwen_inference.py:16-24; request.json note: 'ttft_ms is measured inside infer() ... terminated by torch.cuda.synchronize()').

The model must be Qwen3ForCausalLM loaded from the frozen assets path (revision directory 1cfa9a7208912126459214e8b04321603b3df60c) in bfloat16 with attn_implementation='sdpa', eval mode, local_files_only=True (qwen_inference.py:49; request.json model/precision policy note); architecture, precision, attention implementation and weights are unchanged.

Numerical policy from common.configure(): torch.set_num_threads(4), set_num_interop_threads(1), torch.manual_seed(20261020), matmul and cudnn TF32 disabled, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', cudnn.benchmark False (common.py:34-42; request.json note).

Inputs are constructed from the workloads.json qwen_inference.prompt via the tokenizer's chat template with add_generation_prompt=True and enable_thinking=False, encoded without special tokens, repeated/truncated to exactly prompt_tokens=256 and tiled to batch=1, resident on the worker device (qwen_inference.py:55-58; request.json input-construction note).

Source-defined correctness must hold per invocation: a teacher-forced replay must satisfy torch.equal(actual_tokens, tokens) for the full 32 greedy tokens, per-step last-position logits must match the greedy capture within logits_atol=logits_rtol=0.02, and a +1 corrupted reference must be rejected; these relational checks are implemented in observe() outside timed run() (qwen_inference.py:59-64; workloads.json qwen_inference.correctness; request.json quality).

The timed region contains only one clean infer() call; model/tokenizer loading, tokenization, reference construction, teacher-forced verification, negative control, torch.save, warmup, repeats and statistical reduction are outside it (request.json notes on harness vs measured invocation).

Workload dimensions (batch=1, prompt_tokens=256, new_tokens=32) are read from request['workload'] in prepare(); they are frozen for this run but a separately validated variant may supply different values through the same adapter (request.json workload; adapter contract).

Single-process, single-GPU task: the adapter uses context['device'] after worker device binding instead of choosing a physical GPU, initializes no process group, and performs no communication (request.json note: single-process single-GPU task, no distributed backend, no communication collector fields required).
assumptions: The worker-supplied context['device'] (e.g. cuda:0) replaces the source's hard-coded common.configure(device=0)/.cuda(); torch.cuda.set_device(context['device']) plus .to(device) place the model and inputs on that same logical device.

The prompt text is task data fixed across workloads: it is read from the bundled source copy at inputs/source/workloads.json (qwen_inference.prompt), with request source_root as a secondary candidate and the exact prompt string embedded as a last-resort fallback; prompt_tokens/batch/new_tokens never fall back and always come from request['workload'].

torch.set_num_interop_threads(1) may raise RuntimeError if the worker process already configured inter-op threads; it is guarded so prepare stays safe, matching common.configure()'s intent rather than its failure mode.

The framework performs warmup/repeats (warmup=2, repeats=5, continuous_steps=2) and median reduction externally with measurement_lifetime 'invocation'; run() is exactly one clean infer() invocation, so the source's summarize()/median harness responsibility transfers to the framework.

In quality mode run() retains per-step last-position logits exactly like source capture=True; in measure/profile mode it follows the clean capture=False path. Both paths execute identical forwards and the same 32-token work; capture only keeps references to logits the forward already produced.

The teacher-forced verification rerun and the +1 corruption control execute in observe() outside the timed region, mirroring the source harness (qwen_inference.py:59-64); logits comparisons use the request's logits_atol/logits_rtol (0.02).

peak_allocated_bytes is queried in metrics() outside the timer (the framework resets CUDA peak stats at its own boundary), replacing the source harness's per-sample query; it is a recorded diagnostic, not an objective or constraint for this request.

The workload's second goal (decode_tokens_per_second, max) is reported as a source metric computed with the source formula batch*(new_tokens-1)/decode_window over the 31 decode tokens, but this request optimizes only ttft_ms (request.json note); the held-out 'long_prompt' workload in workloads.json is not part of this frozen request.

Internal phase timings keep the source's perf_counter_ns clock so ttft_ms reproduces the source's measurement semantics, while the framework's wall clock wraps the whole run(); both are exposed separately in metrics().

reset() deliberately performs no gc.collect()/torch.cuda.empty_cache(), because the source's repeat loop runs consecutive timed infer() calls without clearing the allocator; clearing happens in the harness only before the warmup block, and capture references are dropped instead.
